headline: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: Bill 116 would let the mayor sign an agreement with the State of Hawaiʻi School Facilities Authority for temporary wastewater service to a new Central Maui school.
meeting.recap: Bill 116 would let the mayor sign an agreement with the State of Hawaiʻi School Facilities Authority for temporary wastewater service to a new Central Maui school.[[0:10:30]] The school is expected to open in 2031.[[0:10:52]] The County's new Central Maui wastewater plant is projected to start operating in late 2029.[[0:10:52]] If the new plant isn't ready, the school could use up to 14,500 gallons a day at the existing plant.[[0:11:05]] A testifier asked members to advance $1.8 million for design work on UV disinfection.[[0:18:05]] The testifier said no flow should be added to that plant until it has effective disinfection.[[0:20:21]] The committee approved an amendment fixing the existing plant's name in the bill, nine ayes to zero noes.[[0:31:07]]
meeting.next: Written testimony will continue to be accepted into the record.

moments.q: "But it's kind of just a Plan B."

trackerIssues.title: Disinfecting wastewater that reaches the ocean

issues.oneLine: A bill would set up temporary wastewater service for a new Central Maui school.
issues.brief: The school could use up to 14,500 gallons per day at the existing plant, subject to available capacity.[[#1]] The director said the new plant has its environmental permits and is working through land approvals.[[#2]] The director confirmed the 14.9-acre plant site does not need the Land Use Commission because it is under 15 acres.[[#3]] A testifier warned against adding flow to the existing plant before it has effective disinfection.[[#4]]
